title: Main idea of a fiction or poetry excerpt
subtitle: Central Ideas and Details · 22 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **22 of the official questions in Central Ideas and Details are this one** — 11 Easy, 5 Medium, 6 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- A line in italics introduces a novel, story, memoir or poem ('The following text is adapted from...'), and the stem asks for the main idea.
- The choices describe what a character or speaker is doing, feeling or regretting.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Use the italic introduction to learn who is involved and what the situation is.
- 2) Follow the character's or speaker's emotion or action from start to end, looking for words of tone such as pleased, lost, unable, wish.
- 3) Pick the choice that matches both the situation and that emotional direction.
- For poems, restate the whole thing in plain English first, including any 'then, and only then' turn at the end.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices reverse the tone (bored when the character is absorbed, celebrating when the speaker regrets) or add a motive the text never gives, such as hiding or avoiding something.
In poems, you get caught by a choice that describes only the images from the first stanza and misses the reflection the poem turns to.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The wrong choices reverse the tone (bored when the character is absorbed, celebrating when the speaker regrets) or add a motive the text never gives, such as hiding or avoiding something.
In poems, you get caught by a choice that describes only the images from the first stanza and misses the reflection the poem turns to.
